chains.title: Ref (C; = G on the LMO1 sense strand) creates a GATA3 site in the LMO1 intron-1 enhancer, driving LMO1 expression in adrenergic neuroblastoma cells
chains.element: LMO1 intron 1 / super-enhancer element at chr11:8233861
chains.cell_type: Adrenergic (noradrenergic) neuroblastoma cells, e.g. SK-N-SH / sympathoadrenal neuroblast precursors

links.claim: The ref C allele (G on the opposite strand, the orientation used in the original report) completes a canonical GATA (WGATAA) motif that GATA3 binds; the alt A allele disrupts the core and abolishes binding, so binding is higher on ref.

The variant sits in an intron-1 enhancer of LMO1 that is part of a neuroblastoma super-enhancer marked by H3K27ac and occupied by the adrenergic core regulatory circuit; allele-specific enhancer activity follows the GATA motif.
The enhancer loops to and activates the LMO1 promoter, so the ref allele yields higher LMO1 mRNA in cis (allelic imbalance in heterozygotes).
GATA3 is highly expressed and essential in adrenergic neuroblastoma cells such as SK-N-SH, making the effect cell-type restricted to the sympathoadrenal lineage.
LMO1 is a neuroblastoma oncogene; higher LMO1 from the ref allele increases neuroblastoma risk, and the alt allele is protective.

predictions: GATA3 ChIP-seq/ChIP-qPCR in heterozygous neuroblastoma lines shows strong ref-allele-biased occupancy at chr11:8233861
GATA3 knockdown reduces LMO1 expression and enhancer H3K27ac specifically in lines carrying the ref allele
Reporter assay: ref construct >> alt construct in adrenergic but not mesenchymal or non-neural cells
Allele-specific LMO1 expression in heterozygous tumors favors the ref haplotype
falsified_if: No allelic bias in GATA3 ChIP at the site
GATA3 depletion leaves LMO1 unchanged while another GATA-family or non-GATA factor accounts for the effect
Ref and alt reporters behave identically

chains.title: Null: no TF-binding effect of rs2168101 itself
predictions: No allele-specific ChIP signal for any TF at the site
Reporter constructs for ref and alt are indistinguishable
Any LMO1 association tracks a different variant on the same haplotype after fine-mapping or CRISPR tiling
falsified_if: Clear allele-specific TF occupancy or reporter difference at this exact base
Base editing of only this position changes LMO1 expression

chains.title: Same GATA motif, but GATA2 is the occupying family member
chains.cell_type: Neuroblastoma cells of the sympathoadrenal lineage

links.claim: GATA2 shares the WGATAA specificity; a SELEX-based prediction names the GATA group, not a single TF. Within the group GATA2 is the alternative candidate because it is also expressed in sympathetic neuroblasts; ref binds more, alt disrupts.
The same intron-1 enhancer is bound by GATA2 in some neuroblastoma backgrounds, with ref-allele-preferential occupancy.
GATA2 occupancy activates LMO1 transcription in cis.
GATA2 participates in the sympathoadrenal transcriptional program; effect limited to that lineage.
Elevated LMO1 promotes neuroblastoma, so the ref allele confers risk.

predictions: GATA2, not GATA3, ChIP signal is allele-biased at the site
GATA2 knockdown lowers LMO1 while GATA3 knockdown does not
GATA2 expression in SK-N-SH comparable to or higher than GATA3
falsified_if: GATA2 is not expressed or not bound at the locus in neuroblastoma lines
GATA2 depletion does not change LMO1 while GATA3 depletion does

chains.title: The GATA site acts as the anchor of a GATA/TAL1-type composite complex; TAL1 recruitment is the functional readout

links.claim: TAL1 does not read the GATA core directly but is tethered through a GATA partner at a composite E-box-GATA element; the ref allele supports complex assembly and the alt allele does not, so ref binds more.
The enhancer behaves as a composite element whose activity depends on the intact GATA half-site.
Loss of complex assembly on the alt allele reduces LMO1 transcription.
TAL1-containing complexes with LMO proteins are active in neuroblastoma and related lineages.
Reduced LMO1 on the alt allele lowers neuroblastoma risk.

predictions: TAL1 ChIP shows allele-biased occupancy that is lost upon GATA-factor depletion
An intact adjacent E-box is required for reporter activity
Co-IP shows GATA factor and TAL1 at the locus
falsified_if: No TAL1 occupancy at the element
Reporter activity is unaffected by E-box mutation while GATA mutation abolishes it

matrix.test: Mine existing neuroblastoma GATA3 and GATA2 ChIP-seq plus RNA-seq (e.g. SK-N-SH, Kelly, NGP) for reads overlapping chr11:8233861 and for relative TF expression

outcomes.outcome: GATA3 peak at the site with ref-biased reads; GATA3 >> GATA2 expression
GATA2 peak with ref-biased reads; GATA2 expressed at least as highly as GATA3
GATA peak accompanied by a coincident TAL1 peak
No TF peak, or a peak with no allelic bias in heterozygous lines

matrix.test: Luciferase reporter with ref vs alt 300 bp element in SK-N-SH and a non-neural control line

outcomes.outcome: Ref >> alt in SK-N-SH only
Ref >> alt in SK-N-SH only (indistinguishable from H1)
Ref >> alt and loss of activity when the neighbouring E-box is mutated
No difference between alleles

matrix.test: siRNA/shRNA knockdown of GATA3 vs GATA2 in SK-N-SH, then LMO1 qPCR

outcomes.outcome: LMO1 drops with GATA3 knockdown only
LMO1 drops with GATA2 knockdown only
LMO1 drops with either GATA knockdown and with TAL1 knockdown
LMO1 may drop, but with no allele dependence in heterozygous lines

matrix.test: CRISPR base editing / HDR conversion of C to A at the endogenous site in a heterozygous line, with allele-specific LMO1 qPCR

outcomes.outcome: LMO1 falls from the edited allele
LMO1 falls from the edited allele
LMO1 falls from the edited allele
No change in LMO1

matrix.test: QBiC-SELEX lookup of GATA3 and GATA2 models for this 12-mer context

outcomes.outcome: GATA3 own or mapped model predicts strong ref-preferential binding
GATA2 model predicts the same shared GATA specificity; cannot discriminate within family
No TAL1 effect predicted (indirect tethering)
No significant predicted binding change

next_experiment: Interrogate already-public neuroblastoma GATA3 and GATA2 ChIP-seq plus matched RNA-seq/WGS at chr11:8233861 in heterozygous lines: allele-counted reads tell you whether GATA3 or GATA2 occupies the site and whether occupancy is ref-biased at all, separating H1 from H2 (and from the null) at essentially zero bench cost.
